definitions.explanation: Flat stones laid on the ground to form a path or surface. Used for garden paths, walkways, plazas, and streets.

examples.japanese: ⟦{庭|にわ}→庭：02239_niwa⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧{敷石|しきいし}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{並|なら}べる→並べる：01091_naraberu⟧。
examples.english: To lay paving stones in the garden.

examples.japanese: ⟦{雨|あめ}→雨：00583_ame⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧{敷石|しきいし}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{濡|ぬ}れて→濡れる：00800_nureru⟧⟦{滑|すべ}りやすい→滑りやすい：27611_suberiyasui⟧。
examples.english: The paving stones are wet from the rain and slippery.

examples.japanese: ⟦{古|ふる}い→古い：00488_furui⟧⟦{神社|じんじゃ}→神社：01620_jinja⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{参道|さんどう}→参道：11980_sandou⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{苔|こけ}→苔：04991_koke⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{生|は}えた→生える：02392_haeru⟧{敷石|しきいし}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{続|つづ}いている→続く：00903_tsuzuku⟧。
examples.english: Moss-covered paving stones line the approach to the old shrine.

notes: Composed of ⟦{敷|し}く→敷く：00366_shiku⟧ (to lay, to spread) + ⟦{石|いし}→石：02177_ishi⟧ (stone). Common collocations: {敷石|しきいし}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{敷|し}く→敷く：00366_shiku⟧ (to lay paving stones), {敷石|しきいし}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{道|みち}→道：00505_michi⟧ (a stone-paved path). Found in traditional Japanese gardens, shrine approaches (⟦{参道|さんどう}→参道：11980_sandou⟧), and historical districts. Related: ⟦{石畳|いしだたみ}→石畳：08398_ishidatami⟧ (stone pavement — a broader term for stone-paved surfaces), ⟦{飛|と}び{石|いし}→飛び石：29881_tobiishi⟧ (stepping stones placed at intervals).
